name: Parodi's Hemispingus
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru (cusco)
description: Small olive-yellow tanager with a dingy brown face and crown and a yellow eyebrow. Found in humid elfin forest in the southern Peruvian Andes, where it forages singly or in pairs, often joining mixed-species flocks with other tanagers, flowerpiercers, and hemispinguses.

name: Cameroon Olive-Greenbul
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southeastern nigeria and southwestern cameroon; bioko
description: An active but easily overlooked long-tailed greenbul found in flocks in the understory and along the edges of montane forest. Can be found near ant swarms.

name: Rarotonga Monarch
rangeDescription: Forest undergrowth of rarotonga (southwestern cook islands)
description: A thick-set flycatcher with bicolored plumage, dark above and white below. Body darker than grayish head.

name: Serra do Mar Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of southeastern brazil (espírito santo to northern rio grande do sul)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a long slender tail. Differs from other tyrannulets in being mostly bright olive-green above and gray below with darkish ear patches, prominent white eyerings, and pinkish (not dark) legs.

name: Ruddy Crake
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern mexico to northwestern costa rica (northern guanacaste)
description: A small, elusive bird of freshwater marshes, damp fields, and roadside ditches; heard much more often than seen. Walks quietly and runs quickly, like all rails.

name: River Lapwing
rangeDescription: Rivers of india and nepal to southwestern china and indochina
description: The black, gray, and brown coloration of this medium-sized shorebird makes it unmistakable. Raises black crest when displaying.

name: Bronze Parotia
rangeDescription: North-central new guinea (foja mountains)
description: A fairly large, short-tailed bird of mid-mountane forest canopy in the Foja Mountains. Male is mainly black with white flanks, bronzy-scaled chest and 6 antennalike feathers projecting from the back of the head.

name: Cundinamarca Antpitta
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of colombia (cundinamarca and meta)
description: A rather plain antpitta known only from a small area of Colombia’s eastern Andes, southeast of Bogotá. Plumage is dull brown with small white streaks on the underparts, a slightly paler belly, and a faint eyering.

name: Chinese Bamboo-Partridge
rangeDescription: Arid bush of southern and central china
description: While common in bamboo forest, this loud and colorful partridge can be found in a range of other shrubby and semiopen habitats. Not particularly shy; singing males can be located by their far-carrying song, a rising series of piercing single and triple notes.

name: Blue-billed Teal
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa and madagascar
description: Small brownish duck with a blue bill, dark cap, and a dark smudge on the pale tan cheek. In flight, look for white, black, and green stripes on the wing.

name: Spangled Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northeastern new guinea (montane forest of huon peninsula)
description: A large, common, honeyeater of montane forests on the Huon Peninsular. Blackish with a paler throat and long tail.

name: Sombre Pigeon
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of sulawesi
description: A distinctive, very large gray pigeon with a small patch of red skin around the eye and a barred belly and undertail. Back blackish-gray, head and breast much paler gray.

name: Flammulated Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Pacific lowlands of western mexico (sinaloa to western chiapas)
description: Medium-sized flycatcher of thorn forest and brushy woodland in tropical lowlands and foothills of west Mexico. Mostly sluggish and easily overlooked unless singing; tends to stay within cover rather than coming out into open areas.

name: Collared Bush-Robin
rangeDescription: Mountains of taiwan
description: Male is unmistakable, with a glowing silver supercilium, black hood, and fiery orange shoulder and collar. Female is more somber in plumage, brownish above, buffy below, with a trace of the male's pale brow.

name: Tickell's Thrush
rangeDescription: Himalayas of kashmir to nepal; winters to southern peninsular india
description: Both sexes of this thrush are fairly uniformly-colored: the male is predominantly blue-gray and the female is warm brown with a slight buffy wash to the underparts. May be confused with Indian Blackbird in southwestern wintering range, but both sexes are paler and smaller than their respective counterparts of that species.

name: Nilgiri Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Western ghats and coastal southwestern india
description: Small plain gray-brown bird with a slightly curved bill. Nearly identical to Plain Flowerpecker, but ranges do not overlap.

name: Northern Masked-Weaver
rangeDescription: Sudan, western and southwestern ethiopia, south sudan, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, and western kenya
description: A fairly small, slim weaver with a chunky bill. Always shows a dark bill and eye.

name: Rufous-backed Redstart
rangeDescription: Montane forest of central asia; winters to iran and northern india
description: Stunning male has black mask, silvery cap, white wing patches, and bright orange back and underparts. Female is grayish-brown with paler underparts, fainter wingbars, a rufous tail, and a weak eye-ring.

name: Cayenne Jay
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela (bolívar) to the guianas and northeastern brazil
description: Large jay of humid forest and edges including savanna and premontane forest in the tepui region. Combination of size and black-and-white plumage unlike any other species in range.

name: Crow Honeyeater
rangeDescription: New caledonia
description: Large, mostly black honeyeater that is now rare and local in remnant patches of primary forest. Black plumage accentuated by patches of bright red facial skin.
